messages:
alex (DevEx): Heads up — the new nextjs-llama-starter shows different behavior between SSR and client when using the Redwood SDK. SSR requests from pages/server.js get 403 intermittently. Frontend calls are fine.

ravi (SDK): Any logs or repro steps? SSR path uses our edge runtime fetch polyfill, different auth flow.

alex (DevEx): Repro: checkout ./examples/next-llama-starter, run `yarn dev` and hit /summary?id=abc. Server log: ```
2025-02-11T18:02:11Z GET /summary?id=abc 403 {"message":"missing api key"}
2025-02-11T18:02:11Z middleware auth: got token from secret manager
2025-02-11T18:02:11Z outgoing fetch /v1/generate headers: { }
```
Note: same secret is set and used for client-side calls (via edge /api/proxy) which work.

mei (Eng): Sounds like the SDK's server-side helper isn't injecting the Authorization header when running under Next's edge runtime (or the polyfill strips headers). Which SDK version in the example?

alex (DevEx): example uses "@redwood/inference-sdk": "0.11.2". In server code it's: ```js
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference-sdk'
const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
export async function GET(req) {
  const data = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood/llama-mini', prompt })
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(data))
}
```

ravi (SDK): We added a Node-only KMS token loader in 0.11.x that uses node-fetch headers. Edge runtime requires a different code path because it uses global fetch. Looks like createClient picks node loader then falls back, but header injection race can drop headers for SSR.

sam (QA): I reproduced locally with `next dev --experimental-edge` and saw Authorization missing in the outgoing request. When I wrapped the server handler with a manual header it worked: ```js
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RW_KEY}` } })
```
So it's definitely an SDK/server runtime mismatch.

mei (Eng): Plan: 1) short-term patch in the example README to show an explicit header workaround for pages/server/edge; 2) SDK fix: detect edge runtime (global.EdgeRuntime?) and use fetch-compatible header injection path; 3) add tests for next/edge in the sample harness.

ravi (SDK): Agreed. Also we should surface this as an SDK parity issue: our browser JS + node SDKs are consistent but edge targets diverge. I'll open a canary branch that adds runtime detection and a flagged env var RW_SDK_FORCE_EDGE to force the edge path. Canary will be v0.11.3-edge-canary.

deploy-bot: Vercel Preview generated for branch next-llama-edge-fix (preview: https://next-llama-starter-pr-412.vercel.app) :rocket:

alex (DevEx): Quick UX workaround added to example server file: ```diff
- const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
+ const client = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, forceEdgeHeaders: true }) // workaround for edge
```
I'll add a note in onboarding checklist to try `forceEdgeHeaders` if SSR 403s occur.

ravi (SDK): I'll also add idempotencyKey option for generate() so SSR retries won't cause duplicate outputs if we need to replay. That helps sample apps too.

docs (Docs): Adding a short doc section: "Next.js Edge & SSR: common auth issues" with the workaround and the canary link. Also will call out the difference between client-only and server/edge usage in the starter README.

sam (QA): I'll add an e2e that runs the example in an edge-like environment and asserts outgoing requests include Authorization header. Failing test now is filed as QA-889.

mei (Eng): Timeline: SDK canary today, example PR to bump package.json + README within 24h, e2e and canary vercel preview already up.

alex (DevEx): Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread pinned in devex for a day; will remove once the canary is promoted. If you see similar SSR auth blips, mention this thread. :thread:
